dedupe_keys.name: pysim5g open source techno economic simulator for 4g and 5g deployment

description: pysim5g is an open-source Python framework for the techno-economic assessment of 4G and 5G deployment, written by Edward Oughton and colleagues and described in an IEEE Access paper of 2019. Using a Monte Carlo method, it estimates engineering and economic metrics in one framework: a statistical analysis of radio interference gives system-level performance of cells in different frequency bands, including coexistence of 4G and 5G and millimetre-wave bands, while cost modules quantify the capital and operating cost of ultra-dense 5G networks. One application shown is the comparison of 5G infrastructure sharing strategies between operators. Inputs are site densities, spectrum bands, antenna and power parameters and unit costs; outputs are capacity, coverage probability and cost per user or per area, typically plotted against site density. Coverage: generic scenarios, applied to British settings in the paper. Format and access: Python source on GitHub, free under the MIT licence; dependencies include fiona, shapely, numpy, rtree and pyproj. Caveats: a research code from 2019, set up for Python 3.5 with Travis builds, and not maintained as a package; results depend on the assumed costs. Simulation uses: capacity planning and cost optimisation of mobile networks, and screening of sharing or densification strategies. Related records: the India 4G and 5G universal broadband model is its successor with remote sensing, and the Vienna 5G simulators model link and system levels in more detail.
